questions.question: Which description fits the **Linkage** resource?
options: Identifies two or more records (resource instances) that refer to the same real-world "occurrence".
A collection of error, warning, or information messages that result from a system action.

This resource is used for handling concepts not yet defined in FHIR, narrative-only resources that don't map to an existing resource, and custom resources not appropriate for inclusion in the FHIR specification.
A resource that represents the data of a single raw artifact as digital content accessible in its native format.
questions.explanation: **Linkage**: Identifies two or more records (resource instances) that refer to the same real-world "occurrence". The other descriptions belong to **OperationOutcome**, **Basic**, **Binary**.

questions.question: Which resource matches this definition from the specification? “Identifies two or more records (resource instances) that refer to the same real-world "occurrence".”
questions.explanation: This is the definition of **Linkage** (Foundation › Other).

questions.question: Where does **Linkage** sit in the FHIR R4 resource list?
questions.explanation: **Linkage** is in **Foundation › Other**: Infrastructure for exchange itself: Bundle (a container of resources), Binary (raw files), OperationOutcome (errors and warnings), Parameters (operation inputs and outputs), MessageHeader (messaging) and Subscription (notifications).

questions.question: What is the data type of `Linkage.author`?
questions.explanation: `Linkage.author` (0..1) is `Reference(Practitioner | PractitionerRole | Organization)`: Who is responsible for linkages.
